title: Stratifications and middle-perversity allowable chains
notes: The notes give \(X=X_{2n}\supset X_{2n-2}\supset X_{n-3}\supset\cdots\), locally constant stratum geometry, and \(\dim(\sigma_j\cap X_{2n-i})=j-2i\).
statement: Let \(X\) be a pure complex \(n\)-dimensional variety with a conically locally trivial stratification by even real codimension. For middle perversity \(\bar m(c)=\lfloor(c-2)/2\rfloor\), a PL \(j\)-chain \(\xi\) is allowable if \(\dim(|\xi|\cap X_{2n-c})\le j-c+\bar m(c)\), and its boundary is allowable with \(j\) replaced by \(j-1\). Their chain complex defines \(IH_j^{\bar m}(X)\).
reconstruction: The inequality, boundary condition, dimension convention, and perversity are supplied explicitly; the inconsistent displayed formula is not silently repaired.
fate: Already announced in 1977 and published before this talk: \citet[\S\S1.1,1.3]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection}. The same construction occurs in 1979-484.1.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is standard; the displayed equality and codimension indices are not a correct definition.

title: Poincare duality for intersection homology
notes: \ru{В этих когом. есть двойств. Пуанкаре.}
statement: For a compact oriented real \(d\)-dimensional stratified pseudomanifold and complementary perversities \(\bar p(c)+\bar q(c)=c-2\), the intersection pairing \(IH_j^{\bar p}(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes IH_{d-j}^{\bar q}(X;\mathbb Q)\to\mathbb Q\) is perfect. On complex varieties the even-codimension stratification makes middle perversity self-complementary on the relevant strata.
fate: The duality theorem is \citet[\S3.3]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection}; no new 1980 conjecture is being posed.
present_status: As of November 2026, duality holds with these compactness, orientation, coefficient and perversity qualifications.

title: The nodal union of two spheres and failure of homotopy invariance
notes: Two \(2\)-spheres are joined at one point. Ordinary groups in degrees \(0,1,2\) are \(\mathbb Z,0,\mathbb Z^2\); the MacPherson groups are \(\mathbb Z^2,0,\mathbb Z^2\). A path through the node is forbidden.
statement: Stratify \(X=S^2\vee S^2\) by its node and smooth complement. Middle-perversity intersection homology is the homology of the disjoint normalization \(S^2\sqcup S^2\), hence the displayed groups. Intersection homology is not invariant under arbitrary homotopy equivalence. It is invariant under homeomorphism of suitable pseudomanifolds; the two statements are compatible.
fate: This is the elementary nonnormal-curve model of the allowable-chain theory; topological invariance is \citet[\S\S3.2,6.2]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection}. The group calculation follows directly from the chain restriction.
present_status: As of November 2026, the displayed groups are correct; the example demonstrates failure of ordinary duality, while general failure of homotopy invariance requires the distinction between homotopy and homeomorphism.

title: Intersection cohomology versus L2 cohomology
notes: \ru{Гипотеза: совпадают с \(L_2\)-когомологиями.} Borel’s interest is mentioned, but no metric, domain of the differential, compactification or arithmetic hypothesis is specified.
statement: A precise later specialization is the Zucker comparison: for an arithmetic quotient \(X^\circ=\Gamma\backslash D\) of a Hermitian symmetric domain, its Baily--Borel compactification \(X\), and the metrized local system attached to a finite-dimensional algebraic representation, the sheaf of locally square-integrable forms with square-integrable differential represents the middle intersection complex on \(X\). This is a formulation from the literature, not an assertion that the notebook supplies those hypotheses.
reconstruction: The arithmetic setting and differential domain are explicitly later hypotheses.
fate: \citet[theorem on p.~3]{looijenga1988l2} proves this arithmetic specialization; independent work of Saper--Stern was announced in February 1987 and published in 1990. The missing metric/domain data prevent an exact match of the notebook sentence to that theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the cited specialization is proved. The sentence in the notebook is underdetermined as a general mathematical conjecture and is not entered as a newly open problem.

title: Isolated singularities and Deligne truncation
notes: For one isolated singularity the notes say that above half the dimension the groups agree with ordinary groups, and below it they follow by duality; the next page calls Deligne’s general definition inductive.
statement: For a compact pure complex \(n\)-fold with isolated singularities, rational middle intersection homology satisfies \(IH_j(X)=H_j(X\setminus\Sigma)\) for \(j<n\), \(IH_n(X)=\operatorname{im}[H_n(X\setminus\Sigma)\to H_n(X)]\), and \(IH_j(X)=H_j(X)\) for \(j>n\). In sheaf language the intersection complex is obtained from the constant sheaf on the regular stratum by successive derived direct images and perversity truncations.
reconstruction: The precise isolated-singularity formula and the middle-degree clause are editorial reconstruction.
fate: The sheaf formulation was proposed by Deligne in 1976 and is formalized in \citet[\S\S1--3]{goreskymacpherson1983intersection}; the isolated-singularity formula is the allowable-chain calculation. See also \citet[\S6.1, pp.~158--159]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection} for the isolated-singularity chain computation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the middle-degree image is essential. The notebook alternates homology and cohomology terminology, so the displayed high-degree assertion is read homologically.

title: The weighted curve transform and incidence fiber
notes: An \((n+k-1)\)-parameter family is written \(x_i=\varphi_i(x_1,\xi)\), with positive weight \(\chi\), and \(I_\chi f(\xi)=\int f(x_1,\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n)\chi\,dx_1\). The set of curves through \(x^0\) is \(\Gamma_{x^0}\), of dimension \(k\).
statement: On a domain \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), let a smooth incidence submanifold \(Z\subset D\times\Gamma\), \(\dim\Gamma=n+k-1\), have submersive projections and one-dimensional fibers over \(\Gamma\). Locally write \(x_i=\varphi_i(x_1,\xi)\), \(2\le i\le n\). For \(f\in C_c^\infty(D)\), set \(I_\chi f(\xi)=\int f(x_1,\varphi_2,\ldots,\varphi_n)\chi(x_1,\xi)\,dx_1\). Transversality gives \(\dim\Gamma_x=k\).
fate: The general local framework is in \citet[\S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local}; the \(k=1\) setting is written explicitly in \citet[\S1, equations (1)--(4)]{gelfandgraev1980admissible}, received 16 June 1980 and published in issue 14(4).
present_status: As of November 2026, this is a standard double-fibration transform. The redundant coordinate and parameter indices in the notebook require correction.

title: Local inversion from curves through a point
notes: Find families permitting recovery using integrals over curves through the point or infinitesimally nearby; these are called admissible.
statement: For the preceding incidence family, seek a differential operator on transform data and cycles in \(\Gamma_x\) whose periods recover \(f(x)\), or a nonzero distribution supported at \(x\). Closure of a form on \(\Gamma_x\) alone is insufficient: its relevant period must be nonzero and normalized.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local} explicitly distinguishes closed range forms from nonvanishing inversion periods; it also explains the real/complex distinction. This is the published research program being explained, not evidence of an unsolved theorem with stated quantifiers.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established in the cited admissible settings. No blanket inversion theorem for arbitrary curve families is asserted.

title: Admissible first-order differential forms
notes: \(\mathcal H_xF=\sum a_{ij}(x_1,\xi)\partial_{\xi_j}F\,d\xi_i+F\sum b_i(x_1,\xi)d\xi_i\). Admissibility means that \(\mathcal H_xI_\chi f\) is closed for every \(f\); for \(k>1\) this is said to be the complete definition.
statement: An operator taking data functions to differential one-forms restricted to \(\Gamma_x\) is admissible when \(d_{\Gamma_x}(\mathcal H_x I_\chi f)=0\) for all test functions \(f\). Nontriviality is a separate condition after quotienting exact operators; local recovery also needs a nonzero period.
fate: This is the closed-form approach of \citet[\S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local}. The notebook’s closure criterion is meaningful in dimensions \(k>1\), but does not itself imply an inversion formula.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is mathematically meaningful once the omitted target \(\Gamma_x\) and the distinction from inversion are restored.

title: The one-dimensional incidence case and support at a point
notes: For \(k=1\), every one-form is closed; require \(f\mapsto\int\mathcal H_xI_\chi f\) to be concentrated at \(x\).
statement: For \(\dim\Gamma_x=1\), the published definition requires the period functional to vanish for test functions vanishing near \(x\). In the specific first-order incidence setting of Gelfand--Graev this implies \(L_xI_\chi f=c_x f(x)\). The authors further point out that for real curves the local inversion constant is necessarily zero; the support condition is therefore not itself a nonzero inversion formula.
fate: The exactly contemporary treatment is \citet[\S2, Definition 1 and the following remark]{gelfandgraev1980admissible}; received 16 June 1980, published in issue 14(4). Its point-evaluation conclusion is stronger than the general distribution-theoretic fact that a point-supported distribution can contain delta derivatives.
present_status: As of November 2026, the precise published support condition is established; nonvanishing, the real/complex setting and the choice of cycle remain essential to an inversion assertion.

title: Quotient by trivial exact forms
notes: \(\mathcal H_xF=d(\mu F)\) is called trivial; the quotient by such functionals is important.
statement: For a closed one-cycle \(\gamma\subset\Gamma_x\) and a single-valued smooth \(\mu F\), \(\int_\gamma d(\mu F)=0\). Hence one quotients admissible operators by these exact operators when studying nonzero period functionals.
fate: The exact-form quotient is part of the local integral-geometry construction in \citet[\S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local}; the zero-period assertion is Stokes' theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the quotient removes operators that cannot contribute a period inversion formula.

title: A second-order equation and its dual family
notes: Starting with \(y''=F(x,y,y')\), the notes write a general integral \(y=\varphi(x,\xi,\eta)\), then exchange \((x,y)\) with \((\xi,\eta)\).
statement: A regular scalar second-order ODE determines locally a two-parameter family of solution graphs. Conversely, if \(\det\partial(\varphi,\varphi_x)/\partial(\xi,\eta)\ne0\), the parameters can be eliminated from \(y=\varphi\), \(p=\varphi_x\), producing \(y''=F(x,y,p)\). A dual scalar ODE is obtained by regarding the incident parameters as curves, provided the dual projection has the corresponding nondegeneracy and graph property.
fate: This classical incidence interpretation and duality are treated in \citet[\S\S22--23]{cartan1924projective}. It is an exact subject recurrence of 1976-403.1 and 1976-403.3, not a new 1980 proposal.
present_status: As of November 2026, the correspondence is local; arbitrary two-parameter families can fail the determinant condition.

title: Straightening a family of curves by point transformations
notes: Can the family be reduced to \(\xi x+\eta y=1\) by independent changes in the point and parameter planes?
statement: For a nondegenerate local path geometry, ask whether a local diffeomorphism of the point plane takes its unparametrized paths to projective lines; a separate parameter change merely relabels the paths. The criterion is vanishing of Cartan’s projective curvature invariants for the corresponding second-order ODE. The displayed affine line chart omits lines outside that chart.
fate: Solved in the classical equivalence theory: \citet[\S\S22--24]{cartan1924projective}. The same question is 1976-403.1; the notebook supplies no new unrestricted linearization theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the local criterion is established. A general equation is not point-equivalent to the flat line family.

title: Incidence manifolds and double fibrations
notes: There are maps \(A\to B\), \(A\to\Gamma\), and a pair of projections is required to specify a point of \(A\) uniquely. A hypersurface \(f(z,w)=0\) is considered modulo separate transformations in \(z,w\).
statement: A regular incidence geometry is a smooth submanifold \(Z\subset B\times\Gamma\) with submersive projections. Joint injectivity of two maps \(A\to B,\Gamma\) identifies their points set-theoretically; to identify \(A\) smoothly with a submanifold one also needs an immersion and appropriate embedding condition. Equivalence consists of local product maps \((b,\gamma)\mapsto(F(b),G(\gamma))\) preserving \(Z\).
reconstruction: The embedding hypotheses distinguish the smooth formulation from the set-theoretic uniqueness in the notes.
fate: The differential-equation case is classical in \citet[\S\S22--23]{cartan1924projective}; local integral geometry uses the same incidence organization in \citet[\S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formulation is standard with the regularity conditions made explicit.

title: Homogeneous double fibrations and the intersection stabilizer
notes: Take \(A=G\), \(B=H\backslash G\), and \(\Gamma=K\backslash G\); matrix examples use unitary and triangular subgroups.
statement: For closed subgroups \(H,K\) of a Lie group \(G\), the natural joint map from \(G\) has fibers the left cosets of \(H\cap K\). The effective incidence manifold is \((H\cap K)\backslash G\), with its two quotient maps; the map from \(G\) itself is injective only if \(H\cap K=\{1\}\). Smooth embeddedness of its image needs a further regularity hypothesis.
fate: This is the standard homogeneous incidence construction underlying the local integral-geometric framework of \citet[\S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local}; the stabilizer correction follows directly from equality of the two cosets.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is valid after accounting for the common stabilizer.

title: The hyperbolic and horospherical matrix example
notes: For \(GL(n,\mathbb C)\), unitary and triangular subgroups are proposed; the \(n=2\) case is described as a Lobachevsky plane with horospheres. The choice of subgroup is tentative.
statement: A precise standard model is hyperbolic three-space \(SL(2,\mathbb C)/SU(2)\), with oriented horospheres parametrized by \(SL(2,\mathbb C)/(MN)\), where \(M\) is the compact diagonal subgroup and \(N\) upper unipotent. A full complex Borel subgroup instead parametrizes the sphere at infinity. \(GL(2,\mathbb C)/U(2)\) has real dimension four, so it is not a hyperbolic plane.
reconstruction: The SL(2,C), SU(2), MN formulation is editorial reconstruction of the example, not a transcription.
fate: The group/quotient calculation identifies the classical intended example; it does not identify the notebook’s tentative triangular subgroup with the horosphere stabilizer. Its integral-geometric context is \citet[\S1]{gelfandgindikinshapiro1979local}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the exact example requires the subgroup and dimension corrections stated here.

title: Segre families and separate-coordinate equivalence
notes: The notes cite an Inventiones paper on Segre families, use \(\tau(z,\zeta)=0\), and allow independent holomorphic changes in its two sets of variables and multiplication of \(\tau\) by a nonvanishing factor.
statement: A real-analytic hypersurface in \(\mathbb C^{n+1}\) has a complexified defining equation \(\tau(z,\zeta)=0\). Its fibers over \(\zeta\) form the Segre family. Near a regular nondegenerate point, consider the equivalence of this complex incidence hypersurface under independent biholomorphisms in \(z\) and \(\zeta\). Multiplication by a nonzero function preserves the hypersurface and rescales the contact form \(d_z\tau\) on it.
fate: The exact bibliographic identification is \citet[pp.~135--172]{faran1980segre}. The paper was received 15 November 1979, revised 28 April 1980 and published in June 1980. Publisher metadata, rather than the full proof, was checked.
present_status: As of November 2026, Faran’s article is an exact subject match; no assertion that its detailed normal-form theorem has been independently verified is made.

title: Adapted coframes and the Segre structure group
notes: An adapted coframe \((\theta,\theta^\alpha,\theta_\alpha)\) changes by a block matrix with diagonal blocks \(u,U,V\) and independent \(\theta\)-terms in both families. Several displayed indices and stars are inconsistent.
statement: On a complex manifold of dimension \(2n+1\), an adapted coframe changes as \(\widehat\theta=a\theta\), \(\widehat\theta^\alpha=A^\alpha_\beta\theta^\beta+b^\alpha\theta\), and \(\widehat\theta_\alpha=B_\alpha^\beta\theta_\beta+c_\alpha\theta\), where \(a\ne0\) and \(A,B\) are invertible. This preserves the common hyperplane and its two distinguished rank-\(n\) subbundles. If a normalized Levi pairing is imposed, \(A,B,a\) satisfy its additional compatibility relation; the unnormalized block display alone does not impose it.
fate: The notebook explicitly associates this structure with \citet[pp.~135--172]{faran1980segre}. The corrected coframe action is elementary matrix bookkeeping; the exact normalization used in the article was not read.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unnormalized reduction is well-defined. The defective displayed transformation laws are not literal identities.

title: Frobenius conditions for the two Segre foliations
notes: Both ideals generated by \((\theta,\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^n)\) and by \((\theta,\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n)\) must be closed under exterior differentiation; invariants of curve and surface families are requested.
statement: For an adapted coframe, require \(d\theta,d\theta^\alpha\equiv0\pmod{\theta,\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^n}\), and the analogous condition for the lower-index forms. Frobenius' theorem then gives two local rank-\(n\) foliations. Their transversality and, for a nondegenerate Segre geometry, nondegeneracy of the Levi pairing must also be required. The request for invariants is an equivalence problem, not an assertion that every such structure is flat.
fate: The integrability implication is the classical Frobenius theorem; the intended equivalence problem is the published subject of \citet[pp.~135--172]{faran1980segre}, with the ODE antecedent in \citet[\S\S22--24]{cartan1924projective}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the local foliation criterion is established; no separate precise unresolved invariant problem is specified.

title: A G-structure as a reduction of the frame bundle
notes: For a smooth \(n\)-manifold \(M\), its tangent frame bundle is a principal \(GL(n,\mathbb R)\)-bundle; a \(G\)-subbundle is called a \(G\)-structure.
statement: For a closed Lie subgroup \(G\subset GL(n,\mathbb R)\), a smooth \(G\)-structure is a principal \(G\)-subbundle of the frame bundle \(F(M)\), equivalently a reduction of its structure group. Integrability or flatness is an additional condition.
fate: This is classical structure-group language underlying Cartan’s equivalence method; compare \citet[\S\S22--24]{cartan1924projective} for the projective-equation example discussed the previous week.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is standard and supplies no new classification theorem.

title: Geometries on the two-sphere associated with subgroups
notes: The problem is to consider all geometries on \(S^2\) associated with different subgroups \(G\subset GL(n,\mathbb R)\).
statement: For \(S^2\), a reduction question must use \(G\subset GL(2,\mathbb R)\). One can ask which such reductions exist, classify the reductions up to bundle isomorphism or diffeomorphism, or classify locally homogeneous integrable structures; these are different problems. The notes do not choose one, restrict the subgroups, or state an equivalence relation.
fate: No determinate classification problem can be extracted from the single sentence; the neighboring definition identifies the subject but not its quantifiers.
present_status: As of November 2026, this remains an underspecified program in the source, not evidence of an open or undeveloped theorem.

title: Allowability revisited with complex-dimensional skeleta
notes: Fuchs writes \(\dim(\sigma^q\cap X_{n-i})\le q-i\), explicitly noting real codimension \(2i\). He contrasts this with bounds \(q\) and \(q-2i\).
statement: For middle perversity and a stratum of real codimension \(2i\), the bound is \(q-2i+\bar m(2i)=q-i-1\), with the analogous boundary condition. The unrestricted \(q\) condition gives ordinary chains; the transverse \(q-2i\) condition is zero perversity. Its relation to ordinary cohomology uses duality and the normality and compact-support conventions, rather than a literal equality of arbitrary chain complexes.
fate: Compare \citet[\S\S1.1,1.3,3.3]{goreskymacpherson1980intersection} and the earlier occurrences 1979-484.1 and 1980-490.1. The repeated formula is another faithfully recorded missing-index error.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theory is established, but the displayed middle bound differs by one from middle perversity.
speaker: D. B. Fuchs

title: Sheaf-local intersection cohomology and its arithmetic motivation
notes: Deligne wants a definition valid over finite fields; a local complex of sheaves should compute MacPherson’s groups. The comparison with \(L^2\) forms on the smooth locus is again mentioned.
statement: The intersection complex is specified locally by extension and truncation from the regular stratum. This sheaf formulation admits an \(\ell\)-adic analogue over a field of characteristic different from \(\ell\). A proposed \(L^2\) identification is a separate analytic problem and requires a metric and a differential domain.
fate: Deligne’s sheaf construction predates the seminar and is treated in \citet[\S\S1--3]{goreskymacpherson1983intersection}. The precise arithmetic analytic specialization is \citet[p.~3]{looijenga1988l2}. This repeats 1980-490.4--5 rather than supplying a new complete conjecture.
present_status: As of November 2026, the sheaf formulation is established. The notebook’s unrestricted analytic comparison remains underdetermined.
speaker: D. B. Fuchs and A. A. Beilinson

title: Embedding a singular variety and the delta-module picture
notes: Embed \(X\) in smooth \(Y\), regard functions on \(X_{\rm reg}\) as differential equations, and extend them transversely by delta functions. A cross in the plane illustrates the construction.
statement: If \(i:U\hookrightarrow V\) is a smooth closed embedding, the direct image \(i_+\mathcal O_U\) is a holonomic \(\mathcal D_V\)-module supported on \(U\); locally it includes all normal derivatives of a delta generator. For \(U=X_{\rm reg}\), this is first formed on \(V=Y\setminus X_{\rm sing}\), then extended across the omitted locus.
fate: This is the direct-image and support formalism of holonomic systems used in \citet[\S5 and the references there]{kashiwara1984riemann}; its regular-system formulation was already circulated before the talk, as \citet[pp.~XIX.1--2]{kashiwara1980constructible} records on 22 April 1980.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established; a single informal delta function must be read as its generated D-module.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Minimal extension and the irreducibility hypothesis
notes: After maximal direct image the notes assert that there is a unique irreducible submodule; this is the desired extension across the singularities.
statement: For a connected smooth dense stratum \(U\) of an irreducible variety \(X\), an irreducible regular connection has a unique intermediate extension with no nonzero submodule or quotient supported on \(X\setminus U\). For the trivial rank-one connection this is the intersection-cohomology D-module. If \(X\) is reducible, the direct sum of the componentwise extensions need not be irreducible; the cross drawn in the notes has two components.
fate: The correspondence between simple regular holonomic modules and intersection complexes belongs to the regular Riemann--Hilbert theory announced in \citet[p.~XIX.1]{kashiwara1980constructible} and proved in detail in \citet[\S\S5--7]{kashiwara1984riemann}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the intermediate extension is canonical. The notebook’s unqualified irreducibility is false for its reducible example.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Derived solutions from a locally free resolution
notes: Resolve the D-module by free modules \(F_i\) and apply \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_Y}(F_i,\mathcal O_Y)\); the resulting cohomology is called MacPherson cohomology after a codimension shift.
statement: The resulting sheaf complex computes \(\operatorname{Sol}(\mathcal M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_Y}(\mathcal M,\mathcal O_Y)\), using local resolutions. For the intersection-cohomology D-module supported on a pure \(n\)-dimensional \(X\subset Y\), with \(\dim Y=m\), one has \(\operatorname{Sol}(\mathcal M)[m]\simeq IC_X\), where \(IC_X|_{X_{\rm reg}}=\mathbb C[n]\), for the self-dual trivial local system. Thus unshifted solutions restrict in degree \(m-n\); hypercohomology, not stalk cohomology alone, gives the global groups.
fate: The solution functor and derived equivalence are stated in \citet[p.~XIX.1]{kashiwara1980constructible} and \citet[Introduction and \S6]{kashiwara1984riemann}. The explicit shifts reconcile the source’s codimension remark.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is standard with the local/global and shift conventions stated.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Flat connections and local systems
notes: The simplest systems are locally equivalent to \(\partial u/\partial x_i=0\); their solution sheaves are locally constant, while global solutions may not exist.
statement: On a complex manifold a finite-rank holomorphic vector bundle with integrable connection is locally a constant connection and has a finite-rank local system of horizontal sections. Conversely, tensoring such a local system with \(\mathcal O\) gives the connection. Nontrivial monodromy can make the space of global horizontal sections zero.
fate: This is the nonsingular starting case of \citet[Introduction]{kashiwara1984riemann}; the regular-singular extension was already announced in \citet[p.~XIX.1]{kashiwara1980constructible}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the local and global statements are compatible.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: The regular Riemann--Hilbert correspondence
notes: The notes assert equivalence between regular singular holonomic systems and MacPherson complexes, and attribute the regularity definition to Kashiwara.
statement: On a complex manifold, the solution functor gives an anti-equivalence between the bounded derived category of regular holonomic analytic D-modules and the bounded derived category of complex-constructible sheaves. Under the standard dimension shift, the abelian category corresponds to perverse sheaves. Intersection complexes are the simple objects obtained from irreducible local systems, not all constructible complexes.
reconstruction: The distinction between derived constructible complexes, perverse sheaves and simple intersection complexes is supplied.
fate: An explicit theorem and an inverse-functor construction were announced on 22 April 1980 in \citet[pp.~XIX.1--2]{kashiwara1980constructible}, which also acknowledges Mebkhout’s independent proof. The full paper was received 4 March 1983 and published in 1984: \citet[Main Theorem, \S6]{kashiwara1984riemann}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem is established; identifying every regular system with a single intersection complex would be too restrictive.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Torsion-freeness does not characterize connections
notes: The source defines no torsion by \(f x\ne0\) for every nonzero \(f\in\mathcal D\) and nonzero \(x\in\mathcal M\), then says the system reduces to the locally constant case.
statement: A coherent D-module which is coherent as an \(\mathcal O\)-module on a smooth complex manifold is a finite-rank vector bundle with integrable connection. D-torsion-freeness is not this hypothesis: \(\mathcal O\) itself satisfies \(\partial\cdot1=0\), whereas the rank-one free module \(\mathcal D\) is D-torsion-free and is not a finite-rank connection when the manifold has positive dimension.
fate: The proper finite-rank condition is part of the holonomic-system framework of \citet[\S5]{kashiwara1984riemann}. The two counterexamples directly refute the literal criterion; the manuscript visibly writes \(f\in\mathcal D\), not \(f\in\mathcal O\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the source criterion is false; changing only D-torsion to O-torsion would still not supply O-coherence.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Regular singular equations and logarithmic lattices
notes: A Fuchsian equation is written \(dx/dt=t^{-1}A(t)x\).
statement: A meromorphic connection on a complex curve is regular singular at t=0 when it admits a logarithmic lattice. In a suitable meromorphic frame its system has coefficient \(t^{-1}A(t)\) with A holomorphic near zero. A particular displayed system requires A to have this regularity; an arbitrary meromorphic A does not suffice.
fate: This is classical regular-singular ordinary differential equation theory, part of the regularity framework recalled in \citet[\S5]{kashiwara1984riemann}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the logarithmic-lattice criterion is established; the holomorphic coefficient qualification is required.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Testing higher-dimensional regularity on curves
notes: The notes say that it is sufficient to restrict to a sufficiently regular curve.
statement: Regularity of a meromorphic connection can be tested by requiring regular singular pullbacks on all appropriate smooth analytic curve germs through the boundary. This is a quantified curve criterion; checking one unspecified generic curve is not such a criterion. For general holonomic modules, derived inverse image and the support stratification replace a naive restriction of equations.
fate: The curve-wise formulation is part of the regular holonomic theory summarized in \citet[\S5]{kashiwara1984riemann}; the regularity preprint was already cited by \citet[bibliography, item~2]{kashiwara1980constructible}. The notebook’s quantifier is incomplete.
present_status: As of November 2026, the qualified regularity criterion is established. No unrestricted single-curve test is certified.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Finite length and generically flat simple factors
notes: In the general case every module is said to have a finite filtration with irreducible factors, each a locally constant system away from some subvariety.
statement: Coherent holonomic D-modules have finite length locally in the analytic setting and globally on smooth algebraic varieties of finite type. Each simple factor has irreducible support and is, on a dense smooth open subset of that support, an irreducible connection, interpreted by direct image from the support. Arbitrary D-modules need not have finite length. Restricting to regular holonomic factors gives regular connections and their intermediate extensions.
fate: These are the holonomic-category qualifications underlying \citet[\S5]{kashiwara1984riemann} and the regular derived equivalence announced in \citet[p.~XIX.1]{kashiwara1980constructible}. Infinite direct sums refute the literal assertion for every module.
present_status: As of November 2026, the finite-length theorem is established with coherence and holonomicity; its unrestricted formulation is false.
speaker: A. A. Beilinson

title: Subgroups and normal subgroups of finite symmetry groups
notes: Find all subgroups and normal subgroups of symmetry groups of regular polyhedra and of the symmetric group; these are described as problems for first-year students.
statement: For a specified finite group \(G\), enumerate its subgroups and test normality. For \(S_n\), \(n\ge5\), the normal subgroups are \(1,A_n,S_n\); for \(S_4\), add the normal Klein four group. The small cases must be treated separately. For the Platonic solids one must distinguish rotation groups \(A_4,S_4,A_5\) from full reflection-containing symmetry groups. Enumerating all subgroups of \(S_n\) is a finite problem for each specified \(n\), not a short uniform list.
reconstruction: The explicit normal-subgroup answer and enumeration method are expository annotations; the notebook only sets the exercise.
fate: These are classical finite-group exercises. A complete finite enumeration can start at the trivial subgroup and repeatedly adjoin elements until no new subgroup is obtained; every subgroup is eventually reached by its finite generating list. The source supplies neither a value of n nor the rotation/full-symmetry convention.
present_status: As of November 2026, the normal-subgroup assertion and finite enumeration are established; no new finite-group conjecture is posed.

title: Topology of SL(2,R) and its universal covering manifold
notes: Is \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) simply connected? A quadratic change of coordinates gives \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\simeq S^1\times\mathbb R^2\).
statement: The Iwasawa decomposition \(SL(2,\mathbb R)=KAN\), with \(K=SO(2)\), positive diagonal \(A\simeq\mathbb R\), and upper unipotent \(N\simeq\mathbb R\), is a diffeomorphism of manifolds. Hence \(\pi_1SL(2,\mathbb R)\simeq\mathbb Z\), and its universal cover is diffeomorphic to \(\mathbb R^3\). The product decomposition is not a direct-product decomposition of Lie groups.
fate: This classical covering structure is used explicitly in \citet[\S4.2]{belgunmoroianu2025projective}; the notebook already supplies a direct quadratic-coordinate proof of the manifold decomposition.
present_status: As of November 2026, the question has the stated negative answer, with infinite cyclic fundamental group.

title: The universal covering group and a triple-line cocycle
notes: Pairs \((g,n)\) are multiplied with a triple-line index correction. The display writes \(g\in SL(2,\mathbb C)\), then defines a phase using signs of real matrix entries; the kernel of a phase condition is said to have four components, from which the connected one is taken.
statement: The universal covering group of \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) can be defined by homotopy classes relative endpoints of paths from the identity, with pointwise path multiplication. Its kernel is \(\mathbb Z\). Choosing a section gives an integer cocycle \(c(g,h)\), and \((g,m)(h,n)=(gh,m+n+c(g,h))\). A triple-line index can express a cohomologous cocycle only after degenerate triples, normalization, coboundary and topology have been specified.
reconstruction: The path-group construction is supplied to separate the identified object from an unverified explicit cocycle.
fate: The lift-action description is classical and is made precise in \citet[\S4.2]{belgunmoroianu2025projective}. The path formulation reconstructs the intended covering group; it does not certify the notebook’s incomplete phase/cocycle normalization.
present_status: As of November 2026, the covering group is established. The literal SL(2,C), real sign formulas and component assertions do not define that group without correction.

title: Countably many projective structures on the real line up to isomorphism
notes: Kirillov asks for all atlases on \(\mathbb R\) with fractional-linear transitions and says there are countably many structures. The affine line and coverings of the projective line are examples.
statement: Up to projective diffeomorphism, connected open one-dimensional real projective manifolds have countably many isomorphism classes. A developing map identifies one with an interval in \(\widetilde{\mathbb RP^1}\simeq\mathbb R\). Up to lifted projective transformations and orientation reversal, the classes are the full cover, a half-line, and bounded intervals indexed by positive half-integral winding number. If equivalence instead means compatible atlases on a fixed underlying line, without quotienting by diffeomorphisms, the countability statement is false.
fate: The classification is traced to Kuiper (1954) in \citet[Proposition 4.15 and Corollary 4.16]{belgunmoroianu2025projective}; that primary 2025 preprint explicitly recovers the countable open-curve classification while correcting separate closed-curve issues. This differs from the circle problem in 1976-403.6.
present_status: As of November 2026, the countability assertion is proved under projective-isomorphism equivalence; this is a resolved classification problem.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov

title: Levi-flat filling of an embedded two-sphere
notes: Find a Levi-flat three-dimensional manifold \(M\subset\mathbb C^2\) with \(\partial M=S^2\), foliated by complex curves. The drawing shows a one-parameter family of discs with two end points.
statement: A precise proved version assumes a smooth embedded sphere in the boundary of a strictly pseudoconvex domain in \(\mathbb C^2\), exactly two elliptic complex points, and total reality elsewhere. It bounds a Levi-flat hypersurface foliated by analytic discs, smooth up to the sphere away from the elliptic points. The notebook does not state these hypotheses; arbitrary embedded two-spheres need not admit such a filling.
reconstruction: Strict pseudoconvexity and the two elliptic-point assumptions come from the later published theorem, not the manuscript.
fate: The closely matching speaker publication is Bedford--Gaveau (1983), identified in the primary account \citet[Introduction, p.~516]{gaussiersukhov2011filling}, which states its hypotheses and theorem. The same paper’s Theorem 1.1 gives a later almost-complex extension and notes counterexamples without pseudoconvexity. The 1983 original was identified bibliographically rather than read in full.
present_status: As of November 2026, the specified sphere theorem is established; a universal assertion for arbitrary embedded spheres is false.

title: The asserted obstruction for a torus
notes: The parenthetical sentence says that this problem cannot be solved for a torus.
statement: There is no obstruction based only on torus topology: \(M=\{(z,w):|z|\le1,\ |w|=1\}\subset\mathbb C^2\) is a smooth solid torus with boundary the Clifford torus. Its interior is Levi-flat and is foliated by the discs \(w=\mathrm{constant}\). A prohibition would need additional embedding, hull or boundary conditions absent from the notes.
fate: The explicit product example is an elementary expository counterexample. The sphere-filling theorem in \citet[Introduction]{gaussiersukhov2011filling} does not imply a universal nonfilling theorem for tori.
present_status: As of November 2026, the literal torus assertion is false.

title: A degenerate boundary problem of index zero
notes: An isolated foliation singularity is said to lead to a degenerate Riemann problem of index zero, hence solvability; an integro-differential equation is mentioned.
statement: Index zero alone states equality of kernel and cokernel dimensions for a Fredholm operator; it does not imply surjectivity. The notes do not specify the operator, domain, boundary regularity, ellipticity or a separate uniqueness argument, so no definite solvability theorem can be recovered.
fate: The adjacent Levi-flat discussion identifies the area, but the displayed implication has no recoverable hypotheses or operator. Searches for the Bedford--Gaveau filling work did not identify this exact analytic step.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an unrecoverable assertion as recorded; index zero without a kernel calculation is insufficient.

title: Gauge-invariant functional integration as a regularized program
notes: The formal density is \(\exp(-\int\operatorname{Tr}(\Omega\Omega))D\omega\), and gauge transformations act by \(g^{-1}dg+g^{-1}\omega g\). A functional integral on trajectories is proposed.
statement: For a principal compact-group bundle over a compact Riemannian manifold, the gauge action on connections is \(A^g=g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg\), and the Yang--Mills energy is \(\int|F_A|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}\), using an invariant positive inner product. The symbol \(DA\) is formal. The identified construction replaces it by a stochastic process with fixed positive smoothing parameter; it is not a construction of a translation-invariant infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure or of a cutoff-free four-dimensional Yang--Mills theory.
fate: Gaveau--Trauber’s connection-space construction appeared in JFA 38 (1980), 324--341, after a 1979 C. R. announcement. The author’s primary follow-up \citet[Introduction and references 2,5]{gaveaumazet1981elliptic} describes that result and the separate 1980 cutoff quantization announcement. It explicitly acknowledges the Moscow and Leningrad autumn-1980 seminars.
present_status: As of November 2026, the regularized construction is identified; no claim about removing the cutoff follows from these notes.

title: Covariant Hodge heat kernels as diffusion covariance
notes: For a connection \(\Pi\), define \(\Box_\Pi=d_\Pi^*d_\Pi+d_\Pi d_\Pi^*\), use its heat kernel at fixed \(\tau\), and contract it with the second functional derivative of a functional.
statement: On adjoint-bundle-valued one-forms over a compact Riemannian base, \(\Box_A\) is a nonnegative self-adjoint elliptic operator. For \(\tau>0\), \(Q_A=e^{-\tau\Box_A}\) is smoothing and trace class. For smooth cylindrical \(\Phi\), \(L\Phi(A)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(Q_A D^2\Phi(A))\) is a well-defined second-order expression. Gauge covariance of \(\Box_A\) implies covariance of its heat kernel and invariance of this expression.
fate: The exact construction is Gaveau--Trauber (1980), described by the authors in \citet[pp.~105--106 and \S2]{gaveaumazet1981elliptic}; the latter explicitly says that the connection-space operator uses the heat kernel as its symbol.
present_status: As of November 2026, the fixed-cutoff cylindrical generator is established. Its stochastic realization needs the regularity and lifetime hypotheses considered separately.

title: Heat-kernel regularity and the stochastic differential equation
notes: The heat operators satisfy a Hilbert--Schmidt Lipschitz estimate in a \(C^{k,\alpha}\) connection norm. The notes write \(d\Pi_t=e^{-\tau\Box_\tau}d\beta_t\), using white noise; Sobolev spaces are said not to work.
statement: For compact base, fixed positive \(\tau\), sufficient coefficient regularity, and a bounded neighborhood of connections, parabolic estimates give local Lipschitz dependence of smoothing heat operators in suitable operator norms. A local stochastic equation uses the current connection \(A_t\), and a noise coefficient \(e^{-\tau\Box_{A_t}/2}\) has covariance \(e^{-\tau\Box_{A_t}}\). With coefficient \(e^{-\tau\Box_{A_t}}\), the covariance is instead \(e^{-2\tau\Box_{A_t}}\); the It\^o generator has the factor \(1/2\). The construction does not imply that every possible Sobolev formulation is impossible.
fate: The method is described in \citet[Introduction, \S3, Theorem 2 and its proof]{gaveaumazet1981elliptic}, referring back to Gaveau--Trauber (1980), \S\S2--3. The opened follow-up proves its analogous loop-space diffusion up to its lifetime, not an unconditional global theorem for the notebook equation.
present_status: As of November 2026, the regularized local construction is identified; global lifetime, the exact Banach-space norm and the cutoff normalization are not supplied by the manuscript.

title: The Feynman--Kac representation of a Schroedinger semigroup
notes: The expectation \(\mathbb E_x[f(B_t)\exp(-\int_0^tV(B_s)ds)]\) is the evolution operator for \(-\tfrac12\Delta+V\).
statement: For Brownian motion with generator \(\tfrac12\Delta\) and bounded real V, \(e^{-tH}f(x)=\mathbb E_x[f(B_t)\exp(-\int_0^tV(B_s)ds)]\), where \(H=-\tfrac12\Delta+V\). The equality extends to suitable Kato-class potentials, with the operator defined by its closed semibounded quadratic form. The bounded-potential version already makes the displayed formula precise.
fate: This is the classical Feynman--Kac formula; \citet[formula (A26), Theorem A.2.7]{simon1982semigroups} treats it systematically. The later survey is a verification source, not a post-1980 priority claim.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formula is established with the specified operator sign and potential hypotheses.

title: Khasminskii exponential bound and the missing negative part
notes: The displayed assumption is \(|\Delta^{-1}V|\le C<1\), followed by \[\mathbb E_x\exp(-\int_0^\infty V(B_s)ds)\le(1-C)^{-1}.\]
statement: For a Markov process and \(W\ge0\), if \(\sup_x\mathbb E_x\int_0^T W(B_s)ds\le C<1\), then \(\sup_x\mathbb E_x\exp(\int_0^TW(B_s)ds)\le(1-C)^{-1}\). The infinite-time version follows when the same occupation bound holds with \(T=\infty\). For the notebook’s sign take \(W=V_-\). A bound on the absolute value of the Green potential of signed \(V\) permits cancellations and is not this hypothesis; the Green operator must also match the Brownian normalization.
fate: The estimate is the classical Khasminskii lemma; see \citet[Lemma B.1.2, p.~461]{simon1982semigroups}. Expanding the exponential and applying the Markov property bounds its ordered-integral term of order \(n\) by \(C^n\), yielding the geometric series.
present_status: As of November 2026, the corrected bound is established. The signed Green-potential condition as written is insufficient.

title: Large-time logarithmic growth and the bottom of the spectrum
notes: The logarithmic expectation divided by t is asserted to approach \(\pm\lambda_1\).
statement: On a compact connected Riemannian manifold, for continuous real V and \(H=-\tfrac12\Delta+V\), the positive ground state gives \(\lim_{t\to\infty}t^{-1}\log\mathbb E_x\exp(-\int_0^tV(B_s)ds)=-\lambda_0(H)\). A noncompact version needs additional potential, spectral and pointwise-growth hypotheses; the compact formulation is an explicit safe specialization, not a claim that the notes stated compactness.
reconstruction: Compactness and connectedness are supplied as an explicit sufficient setting; no claim is made that they were present in the notebook.
fate: The spectral-semigroup mechanism is classical; compare \citet[\S B.5]{simon1982semigroups}. The sign follows from \(e^{-tH}\), and is not an independent plus-or-minus choice.
present_status: As of November 2026, the compact-case limit holds. The source’s unspecified noncompact generality is not certified.

title: Enveloping algebras and their quotient division rings
notes: The analogue of the group algebra for a Lie algebra is its enveloping algebra; there are many such algebras, and no Wedderburn theorem is available in the intended sense.
statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) over a characteristic-zero field, \(U(\mathfrak g)\) is a noetherian domain and has an Ore quotient division ring. The usual Wedderburn structure theorem for finite-dimensional semisimple associative algebras does not classify these infinite-dimensional algebras. Comparing their quotient division rings is a noncommutative birational classification problem.
reconstruction: The finite-dimensional and characteristic-zero hypotheses and the intended meaning of the Wedderburn comparison are supplied.
fate: This is the framework of \citet[Introduction, pp.~5--6]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}, already discussed in 1967-144.5--6. The statement that there is no Wedderburn theorem is interpreted as a limitation of that finite-dimensional theorem, not a claim that no structure theorem can exist.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Ore construction and birational formulation are established.

title: The unextended Gelfand--Kirillov conjecture revisited
notes: The skew field of fractions of an enveloping algebra is identified with that of a ring of differential operators; Gelfand calls this unfinished.
statement: For a finite-dimensional algebraic Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) over an algebraically closed field \(k\) of characteristic zero, the original conjecture asks whether \(\operatorname{Frac}U(\mathfrak g)\simeq\operatorname{Frac}A_m(k(t_1,\ldots,t_r))\) for some \(m,r\ge0\), where \(A_m\) is a Weyl algebra and the \(t_i\) are central algebraically independent variables. An isomorphism after a finite extension of the center is a different, weaker assertion.
fate: The exact recurrence is GP-1967-21 (1967-144.7); see \citet[Introduction]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}. The finite-central-extension result of \citet{gelfandkirillov1969structure} must be kept separate. \citet[Theorem~1.1]{premet2010modular} excludes simple types \(B_n\) for \(n\ge3\), \(D_n\) for \(n\ge4\), \(E_6,E_7,E_8,F_4\). Type A is positive. \citet[Introduction, pp.~2--3 of the author version]{marianoschwarz2024gelfand} still lists types C and G as unresolved; its version of record appeared in August 2025.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unrestricted conjecture is false. The checked literature through the present search leaves the simple cases \(C_n\), \(n\ge2\), and \(G_2\) open; the necessary-type restriction A, C, G is not a sufficiency theorem. No claimed 2026 resolution of these enveloping-algebra cases was found.

title: Differential operators beyond polynomial coefficients
notes: Polynomial coefficients are said to be insufficient, with partial understanding attributed to Novikov, Krichever and Shabat; an additional name is cancelled.
statement: No class of coefficient functions, differential operators, equivalence relation, or proposed replacement for the Weyl division field is specified. The named researchers suggest the theory of commuting differential operators and integrable systems, but the sentence does not determine a theorem or conjecture in that theory.
fate: The names and the neighboring birational statement are recoverable; a precise publication match cannot be inferred from them. The statement is retained as an identifiable research direction without assigning it an invented finite-gap or spectral-curve theorem.
present_status: As of November 2026, the intended mathematical assertion remains unrecoverable from this source.

title: The BGG sheaf approach on projective space
notes: Bernstein, S. Gelfand and I.M. Gelfand are named in connection with projective space, followed by the instruction to work with sheaves.
statement: The identifiable construction associates to a finite-dimensional graded module over the exterior algebra on an \((n+1)\)-dimensional space a linear complex of vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^n\). In the BGG theorem, the stable category modulo graded free modules is equivalent to \(D^b(\operatorname{Coh}\mathbb P^n)\). This precise statement identifies the named method from its publication; the notebook itself states no categorical equivalence.
reconstruction: The exterior-algebra and derived-category formulation comes from the identified paper, not from the notebook sentence.
fate: \citet[Theorems~1--2, pp.~212--213]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}, submitted 10 January 1978, is the exact author/subject identification. It is also discussed in the previous companion’s records 1977-437 and 1977-438. The November 1980 sentence is a retrospective pointer.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction and equivalence are established. The short pointer cannot be used as evidence that every detail of the published theorem was stated in this intervention.

title: Affine objects and their rings of functions
notes: Affine varieties are uniquely determined by their function rings; the notes then identify a commutative ring with an affine algebraic variety.
statement: Affine schemes are contravariantly equivalent to commutative unital rings via \(A\mapsto\operatorname{Spec}A\). Classical reduced affine varieties over \(\mathbb C\) correspond to finitely generated reduced \(\mathbb C\)-algebras (and to domains if irreducibility is part of the definition). An arbitrary commutative ring is not the coordinate ring of a classical complex affine variety.
fate: The classical affine-variety and coherent-sheaf foundations are \citet[Chapter II]{serre1955coherent}; the notebook moves from that category to the later scheme formulation without marking the change.
present_status: As of November 2026, the ring equivalence is correct in the scheme category; finite generation and reducedness cannot be omitted in the classical variety formulation.

title: Localization of modules and quasi-coherent sheaves
notes: For \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\), the sheaf associated with \(M\) has \(\mathcal M(X_f)=M_f=M\otimes_A A_f\). The affine-open base-change condition is used as the definition of quasi-coherence.
statement: For any \(A\)-module \(M\), the localization rule on principal opens defines a quasi-coherent sheaf \(\widetilde M\). Global sections and sheafification are inverse equivalences between \(A\)-modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on \(\operatorname{Spec}A\). For affine opens \(V\subset U\), a quasi-coherent sheaf satisfies \(\mathcal M(V)=\mathcal O(V)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal M(U)\).
fate: The coherent finite-type version is established in \citet[Chapter II, \S3]{serre1955coherent}; the arbitrary-module quasi-coherent version is its standard affine-scheme extension.
present_status: As of November 2026, the localization construction and equivalence are standard.

title: Serre’s cohomological criterion for affineness
notes: Affineness is characterized by vanishing of higher cohomology and generation of every quasi-coherent sheaf by global sections.
statement: For a separated algebraic variety of finite type, affineness is equivalent to \(H^i(X,\mathcal F)=0\) for every quasi-coherent \(\mathcal F\) and \(i>0\). On an affine variety, the evaluation map \(\mathcal O_X\otimes_{\Gamma\mathcal O_X}\Gamma\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\) is also surjective. Thus the two conditions stated together in the notes are equivalent to affineness in this setting.
fate: This is the affine-cohomology criterion introduced in \citet[Chapter II, \S3]{serre1955coherent}, with the quasi-coherent formulation standard in the scheme setting.
present_status: As of November 2026, the statement is established with the finite-type and separation hypotheses.

title: Quasi-coherent D-modules and D-affinity
notes: A D-module is called quasi-coherent if its underlying O-module is quasi-coherent. D-affinity requires higher-cohomology vanishing and generation by global sections.
statement: For smooth \(X/\mathbb C\), let \(\mathcal D_X\) be finite-order algebraic differential operators and consider left D-modules quasi-coherent over \(\mathcal O_X\). D-affinity means that every such \(\mathcal M\) is acyclic for \(\Gamma\) and the evaluation \(\mathcal D_X\otimes_{\Gamma\mathcal D_X}\Gamma\mathcal M\to\mathcal M\) is surjective. The order of factors records the left-module convention.
fate: This is the localization setting of \citet[pp.~15--18]{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}. Contemporary independent testimony in \citet[p.~44]{brylinski1981differential} explicitly records Beilinson--Bernstein’s stronger vanishing theorem for every quasi-coherent D-module. The November 1980 notes are an early seminar exposition.
present_status: As of November 2026, the definition is standard and supports the categorical equivalence in the sequel.

title: Affine varieties, projective spaces, and the elliptic counterexample
notes: Every affine variety and every projective space is D-affine; an elliptic curve is not.
statement: A smooth affine complex variety is D-affine by ordinary affine quasi-coherent cohomology and generation. Complex \(\mathbb P^N\) is D-affine by localization (or its projective-space case). An elliptic curve \(E\) is not: \(\mathcal O_E\) is a left D-module and \(H^1(E,\mathcal O_E)\ne0\).
fate: The projective assertion is a special case of \citet[pp.~15--18]{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}; its all-module vanishing is independently recorded in \citet[p.~44]{brylinski1981differential}. The affine and elliptic observations are elementary consequences of the definition and earlier coherent cohomology.
present_status: As of November 2026, all three examples have the stated outcomes; the positive-dimensional projective example is the new localization content.

title: Induced D-modules from negative line bundles
notes: Even for \(\mathcal L=\mathcal O(-i)\) on projective space, \(\mathcal D_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L\) is generated by global sections and acyclic. The notes say \(\mathcal O(-i)\) itself has no sections and has higher cohomology.
statement: For quasi-coherent \(\mathcal L\), induction uses the right O-action on \(\mathcal D_X\), producing a left D-module. On D-affine \(X\) it is acyclic and D-generated by its global sections. On \(\mathbb P^N\), \(H^0\mathcal O(-i)=0\) for \(i>0\), while nonzero higher cohomology occurs only for \(i\ge N+1\); for \(1\le i\le N\) all cohomology vanishes. For an invertible \(\mathcal L\), the induced module is locally free of rank one over D.
fate: The induced-module consequence follows directly from the all-module localization theorem recorded in \citet[p.~44]{brylinski1981differential} and \citet{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}; the line-bundle cohomology is classical.
present_status: As of November 2026, the induced-module assertion holds, but the blanket higher-cohomology assertion for every negative twist does not.

title: Reversing the tensor product and formal transposition
notes: The reversed \(\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal D\) has \(\mathcal L\) as a direct summand. An involution of D fixing functions would identify the two constructions. On an elliptic curve formal adjoint is written \(f\partial_x\mapsto\partial_xf\).
statement: The reversed tensor is naturally a right D-module, with the left O-action on D used in forming it. As an O-module, evaluation \(P\mapsto P(1)\) splits \(\mathcal O\hookrightarrow\mathcal D\), so \(\mathcal L\) is a direct summand. Formal transposition reverses order and sends \(\partial_x\mapsto-\partial_x\) in a constant-volume coordinate; globally it exchanges left and right modules via the canonical bundle. It is not an unrestricted canonical involution of the same untwisted ring.
fate: This is the classical left/right duality of differential operators used in \citet[Introduction, formulae for duality]{kashiwara1984riemann}. The source’s missing minus sign already contradicts \([\partial_x,x]=1\).
present_status: As of November 2026, the splitting is correct; the side convention, canonical-bundle twist and adjoint sign are essential.

title: Does equivalence by global sections imply D-affinity?
notes: D-affinity implies that \(\Gamma:\mathcal D_X\text{-mod}\to\Gamma(\mathcal D_X)\text{-mod}\) is an equivalence. The speaker says he does not know the converse.
statement: For the category of O-quasi-coherent left D-modules on a smooth separated finite-type variety, D-affinity is equivalent to the natural adjunction between global sections and localization being an equivalence. In the reverse implication, equivalence gives exactness and detection of nonzero objects; an affine \v{C}ech resolution computes the higher sheaf cohomology.
fate: The notebook itself supplies the converse one week later, in record 498, by the compact projective generator argument. This abstract mechanism is the standard module-category criterion, stated with proof outline in \citet[\S1.2]{keller1997categories}; the localization application is \citet{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the question is answered affirmatively under these hypotheses, including in the next recorded talk.

title: The canonical class obstruction and the limits of Chern-class arguments
notes: Vanishing of the first Chern class of the canonical or tangent bundle is said to imply non-D-affinity and existence of an involution. An insertion identifies line-bundle isomorphism with equality of first Chern classes.
statement: Without properness the non-D-affinity claim is false: affine space has trivial canonical bundle and is D-affine. A safe precise special case is that a smooth connected projective variety of positive dimension with trivial canonical bundle is not D-affine, since \(H^{\dim X}(X,\mathcal O_X)\simeq\mathbb C\) by Serre duality. Equality of first Chern classes does not imply algebraic or holomorphic isomorphism of line bundles: nontrivial degree-zero line bundles on an elliptic curve have the same Chern class as \(\mathcal O\).
fate: The obstruction is an elementary application of coherent duality; the global transpose naturally involves the canonical bundle, as in \citet[Introduction]{kashiwara1984riemann}. The source does not specify whether its Chern class is integral, rational, de Rham or an Atiyah class, so the stronger claimed equivalence is not certified.
present_status: As of November 2026, the unqualified implications are false. The stated projective trivial-canonical case is established; it is not claimed to exhaust the intended theorem.

title: Global operators on the flag variety and localization
notes: For semisimple \(G\) and Borel \(B\), \(X=G/B\) is D-affine and \(\Gamma\mathcal D_X=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_0\), where \(I_0\) is the kernel of the trivial central character. Hence D-modules correspond to representations with that infinitesimal character.
statement: For a connected complex semisimple algebraic group \(G\), put \(X=G/B\) and let \(\chi_{\rm triv}:Z(U\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb C\) be the character on the trivial representation. The infinitesimal action induces \(U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_{\rm triv}\simeq\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_X)\). Global sections and localization give inverse equivalences between O-quasi-coherent left \(\mathcal D_X\)-modules and modules over this central reduction. This uses the exact central character, not merely generalized central-character torsion.
fate: \citet[pp.~15--18]{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation} is the direct speaker publication (1981; seminar exposition November 1980). \citet[theorem on p.~43 and addendum p.~44]{brylinski1981differential}, from the August--September 1980 Toru\'n conference, independently proves the global-ring assertion and records the Beilinson--Bernstein all-module vanishing.
present_status: As of November 2026, the untwisted localization theorem is established. Its regular dominant character convention is fixed here by the trivial representation.

title: The projective-line operator algebra and its central relation
notes: On \(\mathbb P^1\) the operators \(\partial_x,x\partial_x,x^2\partial_x\) generate the algebra; the notes say there is a unique operator commuting with all of them.
statement: The three vector fields span \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\). Their universal enveloping algebra maps onto \(\Gamma(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal D)\), with kernel generated by the Casimir minus its trivial-character scalar. The center of \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) is a polynomial algebra in one Casimir; this means one algebraically independent generator, not one commuting operator. In the global differential-operator quotient the center consists of scalar operators.
fate: The rank-one example already occurs in 1967-144.13. The general quotient description is proved in \citet[p.~43]{brylinski1981differential}; the Harish--Chandra center statement is recalled on p.~45. The generation and relation can also be checked directly in one variable.
present_status: As of November 2026, the example is classical; uniqueness must be read as uniqueness of a central generator up to normalization, not literally a single commuting operator.

title: The Cayley norm and multiplicative composition
notes: In a basis of eight Cayley units, \(\lvert\sum x_je_j\rvert^2=\sum x_j^2\), and \(|ab|=|a||b|\).
statement: The real octonion algebra \(\mathbb O\) is an eight-dimensional unital, nonassociative alternative algebra. Conjugation gives \(N(a)=a\bar a=\sum_{j=1}^8x_j^2\), and \(N(ab)=N(a)N(b)\). Thus its Euclidean norm is multiplicative.
fate: This is the classical Cayley composition algebra; see \citet[\S\S2.1--2.2]{baez2002octonions}. The note asks for a review of its classification, not a newly announced composition law.
present_status: As of November 2026, the norm identity is correct.

title: Dimensions of finite-dimensional absolute-valued algebras
notes: There are none of dimension greater than eight, and in finite dimensions only the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions and Cayley numbers occur.
statement: A nonzero finite-dimensional real algebra with a bilinear product and a multiplicative norm has dimension \(1,2,4\), or \(8\). If it has a two-sided identity, it is isometrically isomorphic to \(\mathbb R,\mathbb C,\mathbb H\), or \(\mathbb O\). Without an identity the dimension assertion remains true, but there are additional isotopes, so the four-algebra isomorphism list is incomplete.
fate: The unital composition classification and its representation-theoretic proof are reviewed in \citet[Theorem~1 and \S2.3]{baez2002octonions}. The reduction of a finite-dimensional absolute-valued algebra to a unital isotope is explicitly proved before Proposition~1 in \citet[pp.~1--2]{kaidiramirezrodriguez1999absolute}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the dimension restriction is established. The unqualified isomorphism classification needs the missing unit hypothesis.

title: The Clifford-algebra route to the dimension restriction
notes: The norm identity gives a representation-theoretic problem and an explicit construction.
statement: For a unital finite-dimensional Euclidean composition algebra A, left multiplication by vectors orthogonal to 1 satisfies \(L_uL_v+L_vL_u=-2\langle u,v\rangle\operatorname{Id}\). Thus A is a module for the real Clifford algebra of its imaginary subspace. Comparing possible module dimensions forces \(\dim A\in\{1,2,4,8\}\); the four usual algebras realize these possibilities. For a nonunital finite-dimensional algebra, pass first to a unital isotope.
reconstruction: The Clifford action and dimension comparison are supplied from the cited account; the source names neither the algebra nor the precise relation.
fate: The explicit representation-theoretic proof is \citet[\S2.3]{baez2002octonions}; the identity is obtained by polarizing the multiplicative Euclidean norm. This is an identification and expansion of the source’s one-line method, not a newly supplied classification proof.
present_status: As of November 2026, the Clifford argument is established and explains the speaker’s reference to representation theory.

title: Can a multiplicative norm exist in infinite dimension?
notes: Gelfand asks whether the multiplicative-norm identity can hold in infinite dimension; Gindikin says yes.
statement: Without a unit, yes: take \(H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)\), choose a bijection \(b:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N\), and define \((x*y)_{b(i,j)}=x_iy_j\). This is a continuous bilinear product with \(\|x*y\|^2=\sum_{i,j}|x_i|^2|y_j|^2=\|x\|^2\|y\|^2\). It has no two-sided identity: under the induced unitary \(H\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}_2H\to H\), the range of multiplication by a nonzero fixed x is the proper subspace corresponding to \(\mathbb Rx\otimes H\). With a two-sided identity, no infinite-dimensional example exists: the Urbanik--Wright theorem gives precisely \(\mathbb R,\mathbb C,\mathbb H,\mathbb O\), without assuming finite dimension or completeness.
reconstruction: The explicit example is supplied from the identified literature, not attributed historically to Gindikin.
fate: The Urbanik--Wright theorem (1960) is stated explicitly in \citet[p.~2, preceding Corollary~1]{kaidiramirezrodriguez1999absolute}. The tensor-coordinate example is precisely the Hilbert-space case of \citet[Proposition~2.2 and Corollary~2.5]{becerramorenorodriguez2005absolute}. Its elementary verification here is an annotation and is not asserted to reproduce Gindikin’s unpublished argument.
present_status: As of November 2026, the question is resolved under either explicit convention. Gindikin’s affirmative answer is consistent with the nonunital reading and inconsistent with the unital one.
speaker: S. G. Gindikin (affirmative answer to Gelfand)

title: Associativity, Desargues, and the Cayley projective plane
notes: After coordinatization, associativity is identified with Desargues; the Cayley projective plane is called the simplest non-Desarguesian example.
statement: For projective planes coordinatized by an alternative division algebra, the plane is Desarguesian precisely when that algebra is associative. The octonionic Moufang plane \(\mathbb OP^2\) is therefore non-Desarguesian. For an arbitrary projective plane, coordinatization uses a planar ternary ring and the bare word associativity is not a complete formulation. Calling the Cayley plane simplest is qualitative, not a minimality theorem.
fate: The construction of \(\mathbb OP^2\), its incidence geometry and its relation to the failure of associativity are reviewed in \citet[\S3]{baez2002octonions}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the division-algebra formulation is established; the source’s shorthand requires the coordinatization category.

title: Differential and locally homogeneous projective planes
notes: It is interesting to study differential and locally homogeneous projective planes.
statement: One could impose smooth point and line manifolds with smooth incidence and join/intersection maps, then ask for transitive or locally transitive collineation groups. The notes do not fix these regularity axioms, the dimension, completeness, the acting group or an equivalence relation, so they specify no unique classification question.
fate: The program is retained because its geometric object is identifiable, but no precise assertion can be reconstructed from this single sentence. The modern study of smooth projective planes does not by itself answer an unspecified classification request.
present_status: As of November 2026, the source remains underdetermined; no new open problem or claim of nondevelopment is inferred.

title: A unified geometric explanation of exceptional Lie types
notes: Classifying Lie algebras is called too particular; the exceptional types \(G_2,E_6,E_7,E_8\) should not appear as isolated fragments.
statement: The request is for a conceptual geometric organization of exceptional Lie theory. Classical octonionic and Jordan-algebra constructions do provide relationships among exceptional groups, but the notebook gives no proposed object, theorem or classification target whose completion can be assessed.
fate: \citet[\S4]{baez2002octonions} supplies a precise later account of octonionic constructions of exceptional Lie algebras. It is a thematic comparison, not evidence for a uniquely recoverable theorem in this source.
present_status: As of November 2026, the mathematical motivation is clear, but an exact assertion is not recoverable. This item is not classified as an undeveloped conjecture.

title: Global sections and localization for a sheaf of rings
notes: Let \(\mathcal A\) contain \(\mathcal O_X\) and be quasi-coherent over it. For \(A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal A)\), the functors are \(\Gamma\) and \(\Delta(M)=\mathcal A\otimes_A M\); the source calls the constant sheaf of M a sheaf of \(\mathcal A\)-modules.
statement: Let X be a separated finite-type complex variety and \(\mathcal A\) a sheaf of unital rings with a given inclusion of \(\mathcal O_X\), quasi-coherent for its left O-action. In the category of left A-sheaves whose underlying O-module is quasi-coherent, localization \(\Delta(M)=\mathcal A\otimes_{\underline A}\underline M\) is left adjoint to global sections. Here \(\underline A\) and \(\underline M\) are constant sheaves, with the natural map \(\underline A\to\mathcal A\). The O-subring need not be central; differential operators are the motivating example.
fate: This is the standard tensor--Hom adjunction used by the projective-generator proof, cf. \citet[\S1.2]{keller1997categories}. It generalizes the affine sheaf/module construction of \citet[Chapter II, \S3]{serre1955coherent}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the adjunction is valid. A general left A-module does not already carry a canonical constant-sheaf action by the varying ring \(\mathcal A\).

title: Cohomological affinity and equivalence of module categories
notes: Two conditions are stated to be equivalent: every quasi-coherent A-module has no higher cohomology and every nonzero one has a nonzero global section; or \(\Gamma,\Delta\) are inverse equivalences. The reverse direction is assigned to the \v{C}ech resolution.
statement: For X and \(\mathcal A\) as in the preceding item, assume the category is closed under the indicated quasi-coherent operations. Vanishing of \(H^{i>0}(X,\mathcal M)\) for every object and detection of nonzero objects by \(\Gamma\) are equivalent to the natural localization/global-sections adjunction being an equivalence. They also imply D-style generation by global sections: the cokernel of the evaluation map is zero. For the converse, use an affine \v{C}ech resolution whose terms and kernels remain in the category.
fate: This explicitly resolves 1980-496.8 and GP-1980-03 in the source itself. The general category-theoretic mechanism is \citet[\S1.2]{keller1997categories}; the D-module application is the setting of \citet{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the criterion is established under the stated quasi-coherent and finite-cover hypotheses. Detection of nonzero objects and exactness, taken together, suffice to recover the generation condition.

title: A compact projective generator identifies an abelian category with modules
notes: An abelian category has arbitrary direct sums and a projective generator P with \(\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)\) preserving them. The notes identify its target as left \(\operatorname{End}(P)\)-modules and write \(\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal A)=A\).
statement: For a locally small abelian category with arbitrary coproducts and a compact projective generator P, \(\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)\) is an equivalence to right modules over \(\operatorname{End}(P)\), or left modules over its opposite ring. Compact means preservation of arbitrary coproducts. For left \(\mathcal A\)-modules, \(\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal A)\simeq\Gamma(X,\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\), so the resulting target is indeed left A-modules. On a quasi-compact separated variety, global sections of quasi-coherent sheaves commute with coproducts.
fate: This classical module-category criterion is stated with its historical attribution and proof outline in \citet[\S1.2, p.~4]{keller1997categories}. The proof takes a presentation by coproducts of P and applies its exact Hom functor. The source has the compactness hypothesis but omits the opposite-ring convention.
present_status: As of November 2026, the lemma is established. The missing opposite ring is a literal error under the explicitly chosen left-module convention.

title: Projective space is D-affine
notes: Theorem (13): \(\mathbb P^N\) is D-affine.
statement: For complex projective space and the sheaf of finite-order algebraic differential operators, every O-quasi-coherent left D-module is acyclic for global sections and is generated as a D-module by them. Consequently the localization/global-sections adjunction is an equivalence.
fate: This repeats the projective-space assertion in 1980-496.5. It follows from the localization theorem of \citet{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}; the all-module vanishing is explicitly recorded in \citet[p.~44]{brylinski1981differential}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem is established; the source means algebraic D-affinity, not ordinary affineness of projective space.

title: Flag-variety localization for a reductive group
notes: For a reductive group G and Borel B, the Lie action gives \(U(\mathfrak g)\to\Gamma\mathcal D_{G/B}\); quotienting by the central annihilator of the trivial representation gives an isomorphism and the expected category equivalence.
statement: For a connected complex reductive algebraic group G, let \(X=G/B\) and let \(I\subset Z(U\mathfrak g)\) be the kernel of the trivial central character. Then X is D-affine and \(U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I\simeq\Gamma(X,\mathcal D_X)\). Thus O-quasi-coherent left D-modules correspond to all left modules over that central reduction. The central Lie algebra of G acts trivially on X and is killed by I; the reductive formulation reduces to the semisimple one.
fate: The exact theorem is \citet[pp.~15--18]{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}; compare \citet[p.~43 and addendum p.~44]{brylinski1981differential}. This is a substantive second occurrence of 1980-496.10, now preceded by the categorical proof.
present_status: As of November 2026, the theorem is established with connectedness and the exact trivial infinitesimal character specified.

title: The transfer bimodule and its two commuting operator actions
notes: The source defines \(\mathcal D_{X\to Y}=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}\mathcal D_Y\), with a left \(D_X\) action by Leibniz and a right pulled-back \(D_Y\) action. The last sentence says df(v) acts on \(f^{-1}\mathcal D_Y\) itself.
statement: For a morphism f of smooth complex algebraic varieties, the displayed tensor is a \((\mathcal D_X,f^{-1}\mathcal D_Y)\)-bimodule. Locally, if \(df(v)=\sum_i a_i\otimes w_i\), then \[v\cdot(b\otimes P)=v(b)\otimes P+\sum_i ba_i\otimes w_iP.\] The right action is multiplication on P. The coefficients \(a_i\) are functions on X, so the formula acts on the tensor product, not generally on the unextended inverse-image sheaf alone.
fate: The transfer-module formula is standard D-module functoriality; see \citet[\S4.3, p.~343]{kashiwara1984riemann}. The notebook captures the correct bimodule but abbreviates the vector-field action too far.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established; \(O_X\) scalar extension is essential to the claimed left action.

title: Derived direct and inverse image in place of a ring pullback
notes: There is no corresponding morphism of rings of differential operators for a general map, but natural functors exist in derived categories; the notes say there are four.
statement: For a morphism of smooth varieties, differential operators do not pull back by a functorial homomorphism of sheaves of rings in the way functions do. Derived inverse and direct image use transfer bimodules and derived tensor products, with the canonical-bundle twist for the reverse transfer module. On the appropriate holonomic derived categories, duality produces the complementary extraordinary operations. Preservation of regularity and comparison with constructible sheaves require the regular-holonomic hypotheses.
fate: These operations are part of the holonomic-system formalism in \citet[\S4.3 and \S8]{kashiwara1984riemann}; the regular derived correspondence was already announced in \citet[p.~XIX.1]{kashiwara1980constructible}. The source does not define four functors on every unbounded module category.
present_status: As of November 2026, the derived functoriality is established, with category and duality restrictions; the notebook’s count of four is a programmatic abbreviation.
